summary: `jarvis offboard <name>` takes a project out of the OS: archive by default (history kept and searchable, re-adoptable) or `--purge --yes`, cancelling its orders, rewriting the catalog, stripping the OS's files from its repo, and dropping it from the running daemon without a restart.

children.title: Make every active-only surface archived-aware
children.description: You add the readers; nobody else may. Write no deletes to central_store or neo_store — sibling `purge` owns those, and you both edit central_store.py around the projects registry, so keep your diff to the new ARCHIVED constant. Do not touch bootstrap.py (`strip`), daemon.py (`daemon`) or add any CLI verb or doc (`offboard`). Nothing yet sets status='archived'; stage it in your tests with set_project_status. Done when an archived project is gone from every active-only surface and still readable through jarvis search and the dashboard, with no existing caller's meaning changed.
children.acceptance: New file tests/test_offboard_registry.py plus additions to tests/test_search.py and tests/test_ui.py. inspect.signature pins the keyword-only `include_archived` default False, and the call writes nothing. With the project active, both call forms return the same dict. project_name_for_path still resolves after archiving. GET /project/proj_a and GET /fo/proj_a/<id> return 200 after archiving and say `archived`; nav_projects omits it; one POST is refused; run_doctor()['os'] shows no INV-UI-HEALTHY violation.

children.title: Delete every trace of a project from os.db and neo.db
children.description: Two functions and their tests, nothing else. No caller exists yet and you do not add one — sibling `offboard` calls you. Do not add the archived status or change any reader (sibling `registry`, which edits the same region of central_store.py: keep your diff to the new methods). Do not touch the per-project database at <project>/.jarvis/jarvis.db or anything in the repo — `strip` removes that directory. A `project` column does NOT mean the row belongs to the project: never DELETE from gate_rules or detectors, which are fleet-wide. Read the section before writing any DELETE.
children.acceptance: A `purge_project` block in tests/test_stores.py. Never deletes from gate_rules or detectors: a gate rule recorded with proj_a provenance still blocks the same command for proj_b after purge_project('proj_a'), with its project now ''; a detector at project='' is untouched and still fires; one naming proj_a is retracted via retract_detector with a reason, never blanked. The pinning test names BOTH lists — nine scope tables, two provenance tables — and their union equals the eleven carrying a project column today, failing with a message saying a new table must be classified before purge touches it; PROVENANCE_TABLES is an explicit constant, not an omission. Seed one row per table through the stores' own writers for proj_a AND proj_b, purge proj_a, assert every proj_b row survives — no hand-written SQL. After purging a knowledge row, search finds nothing and raises nothing. inspect.signature shows no dry_run parameter. An unknown name returns all zeros. tests/test_wo_hide_delete.py stays green.

children.title: Take the OS's files back out of a project's repo
children.description: bootstrap.py only. No caller exists yet and you do not add one — sibling `offboard` calls you. Do not touch central_store, neo_store (siblings `registry` and `purge`), daemon.py (`daemon`) or the CLI. Reuse settings_drift, _tree_matches, tracked_in_vcs and ensure_trust's temp-file write rather than reimplementing any of them, and return BootstrapReport with the same dry_run note convention bootstrap_project already has. Done when a repo offboarded twice reports 'already absent' and still holds every file its owner edited.
children.acceptance: Added to tests/test_bootstrap.py, reusing its spec() helper and _commit_all(); invert test_settings_backup_and_drift and test_a_committed_operation_md_is_never_overwritten. Restores .pre-jarvis and deletes the backup. For a hand-edited settings.json, a committed OPERATION.md and a modified skill tree: bytes unchanged AND report.warnings names it. README.md never removed. The trust entry goes while sibling and top-level keys in ~/.claude.json survive; a malformed one warns and raises nothing. purge=True also removes .jarvis/ and the .gitignore line. dry_run=True with purge=True leaves every st_mtime_ns unchanged — assert this here, nobody else can.

children.title: Stop every order and session a project has in flight
children.description: One ops function plus the central_store methods it needs, which belong beside the backlog and inbox methods, nowhere near the projects registry siblings `registry` and `purge` edit in the same file. No caller exists yet and you add none, and no CLI flag — sibling `offboard` owns the --force deciding whether you write. Reuse ops.cancel and the three cancel_*_order functions; never kill a process. Do not touch bootstrap.py (`strip`) or daemon.py (`daemon`). Queued Morpheus items and unanswered Neo questions are deliberately NOT yours — `daemon` ignores those rather than cancelling them.
children.acceptance: New file tests/test_quiesce.py. Reporting and writing are one function behind a parameter, so section 7's refusal and its --force path cannot disagree: the read-only form leaves a pending order still `pending`. Assert the open set against project_store.OPEN_STATUSES itself, never a literal list, and include a waiting_pr_merge case. A work order, feature order, improvement order and investigation each appear with the right kind and id; cancelling settles all four, children before parents, each with the reason on its record. A seeded queued morpheus_items row and an unanswered neo.db question are still there, untouched.

children.title: Evict an offboarded project from the running fleet
children.description: The hardest piece and the one the feature fails without. You consume ops.registered_project_paths's include_archived parameter, which `registry` ships; you do not change its signature. Do not add ops.offboard_project or the CLI verb (sibling `offboard`), the store deletes (`purge`) or the repo strip (`strip`). Catalog.without_projects lives in catalog.py, which is a stdlib-only leaf and may not read a database — the daemon passes the names in. Daemon.catalog stays a plain attribute; a re-reading property breaks Fleet.reconfigure and the tests that assign it in memory.
children.acceptance: New file tests/test_offboard_live.py. Build the Daemon BEFORE the offboard and prove the precondition with a tick that dispatches — built after, the stamp seeded in __init__ short-circuits the reload and the test passes having reloaded nothing. Then one tick, asserting together: the project gone from daemon.catalog.projects, an unrelated setting from the same catalog write landed, and no `a catalog change was NOT applied` inbox row. A genuinely new project still refuses, word for word. The five uncovered paths each get their own test. INV-OFFBOARDED-ACTIVITY fires for each of its six sources, repairing nothing. `jarvis start --catalog` re-bootstraps nothing — and not under live_daemon.

children.title: Ship the jarvis offboard command
children.description: The join: you call what your four dependencies shipped — ops.quiesce_project, CentralStore/NeoStore.purge_project, bootstrap.unbootstrap_project, registered_project_paths(include_archived=True) — and you are the only child that writes the catalog file or adds a CLI verb. Do not reimplement any of them, do not change their signatures, and do not touch daemon.py (sibling `daemon` owns the live fleet; your catalog rewrite is what its reload_catalog change is for). The nine steps are ordered for safety: quiesce before strip, strip before purge. You ship the documentation too.
children.acceptance: New file tests/test_offboard.py; clear JARVIS_WO_ID or every test fails on the worker refusal. The nine steps run in the section's order, asserted: make the strip fail and the registry and catalog must still have moved together; monkeypatch both and the strip must follow quiesce. --dry-run proven by recorders on all five writers, every one empty — not by a filesystem snapshot, which passes when a dependency ignores its own dry_run. Refusal names the order's id, its status and --force, and nothing moved. After purge, search finds nothing. INV-CONFIG-DRIFT clean afterwards. OS-owning project refused for all four flag combinations, with schedule.os_project asserted as a precondition. Two documentation artifacts ship here too, both specified in the same section 7: a new operator doc docs/os/operator/projects.md covering adopt, offboard, archive versus purge and what each leaves behind, listed in the 'Operating the OS' list of docs/os/index.md; and ONE line in the CLAUDE.md crib sheet directly under `jarvis adopt <path>` — one line, never a section, or the 14 routing scenarios in evals/llm/test_jarvis_judgment.py regress. Tests assert all three exist.
